points.title: Quotation
points.must: Exact words of a source in quotation marks, followed by a citation.

points.title: Paraphrase and summary
points.must: Paraphrase = one idea fully in own words and structure; summary = main points, much shorter; both need a citation.

points.title: Common knowledge
points.must: Widely known facts need no citation; statistics, opinions and findings do.

points.title: When to quote, paraphrase or summarise
points.must: Quote when exact words matter; paraphrase one idea in detail (most common); summarise main points; citation always stays.

points.title: How to paraphrase (worked example)
points.must: Understand, close the source, write from memory, compare with the original, add the citation; patchwriting vs a real paraphrase shown on one passage.

points.title: Referencing: Harvard citation
points.must: In-text (author, year); reference list entry for a book and a web page (with access date); alphabetical order; other styles (numbered, footnotes) — be consistent.

points.title: Copyright
points.must: The exclusive legal right of the author of an original work to copy, distribute, adapt and publish it and to allow or forbid others.

points.title: Why copyright exists; economic and moral rights
points.must: Temporary monopoly so authors can earn; economic rights (reproduce, distribute, publish, translate, adapt, license — can be transferred); moral rights (authorship, integrity — stay with the author).

points.title: Rules of copyright protection
points.must: At least five: automatic, original work, economic and moral rights, life + 70 years, permission / licence needed, ideas not protected, limited free use with source, software protected, consequences.; protected in Kazakhstan by the Law "On Copyright and Related Rights" and the Civil Code.

points.title: Licence, public domain, life of a copyright
points.must: Licence = permission under conditions, not ownership; created → protected during life → 70 years after death → public domain.

points.title: Free use
points.must: Quotation for study, criticism, news; teaching; back-up copy of a program — with author and source, justified amount, no harm to commercial use.

points.title: Creative Commons
points.must: BY, NC, ND, SA (and CC0) with meanings; using others' photos, music and code in a project legally.

points.title: Software licences
points.must: EULA; proprietary, shareware, freeware, open source compared (cost, source code, changes, copies, examples); single-user, volume, site licence, subscription; piracy.

points.title: Copyleft vs permissive; choosing legal software
points.must: GPL: distributed changes stay GPL with source; MIT/Apache: keep the notice; robotics club example — open-source and freeware instead of a cracked copy.

points.title: Plagiarism vs copyright infringement
points.must: Plagiarism = not acknowledging the source (ethical / academic); infringement = using without permission (legal); both can happen together.
